h1: The 7 Best Electric Pruning Shears for Orchards, Roses and Hedges, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Electric Pruning Shears: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless electric pruning shears scored on cutting diameter, battery system, weight, blade change and motor type.
summary: The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch electric pruner is the best pick for most gardeners, with the largest cut among the budget models, two batteries and spare blades. The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX is the easy-to-live-with choice with tool-free blade changes, the CRAFTSMAN V20 fits an existing battery platform, and the Kebtek 40MM suits orchard work.
intro: The cutting diameter on an electric pruner is the number that sells it and the one that misleads most buyers. A shear that is rated for 2 inches will cut a 2 inch branch only when the blade is sharp, the wood is green and the battery is full. Dry hardwood at the same diameter will stall it. Buy a size larger than your thickest regular cut.

Seven cordless electric pruners are ranked below, by cutting diameter, battery system, weight and the practical extras that decide whether a tool gets used. Listings are often terse, and we mark what is unstated. Electric shears do the squeezing for you, but they do not replace a saw for limbs over their rated size.

products.name: ANTTCTIG Electric Pruning Shears, 2.75'' Cut, 2 Batteries & Spare Blades
products.verdict: A 2.75 inch cutting diameter with two batteries and spare blades in the box.
products.description:
The ANTTCTIG offers a 2.75 inch cutting diameter and ships with 2 batteries and spare blades. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It wins on what is in the box. A second battery doubles your working time, which matters in an orchard where the first charge rarely lasts a whole session. Spare blades mean a nicked edge does not end the day. A 2.75 inch rating is the biggest cut among the budget-priced models here. The listing gives no weight or motor type, so we cannot say how tiring it is to hold.

Buy it if you prune thick branches and want to work all afternoon. Skip it if you need the lightest tool.
pros: Largest cut at a moderate price

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX* Cordless Pruner Electric Pruning Shears, 900 Cuts Per Charge, Tool Free Blade Change
products.verdict: 900 cuts per charge, a 20V MAX battery and tool-free blade changes.
products.description:
This BLACK+DECKER is powered by the 20V MAX battery system, rated for 900 cuts per charge, with a tool-free blade change. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Tool-free blade changes matter more than they sound, because a dull or sap-gummed blade is the most common reason pruners stop cutting cleanly, and a change you can do in the garden gets done. The 20V MAX platform means batteries are shared with other tools in the range, which saves money if you already own some. It ranks second because the listing gives no cutting diameter.

Buy it if you own other 20V MAX tools. Skip it if you need a stated cutting capacity.
products.skipIf: You need a stated cut size.

products.name: Kebtek Electric Pruners Cordless Pruning Shear 40MM Professional
products.verdict: A professional-grade 40MM (about 1.6 inch) cutter for orchards and vineyards.
products.description:
The Kebtek Professional cuts up to 40MM, roughly 1.6 inches, and is marketed for professional use. It lands in the priciest tier.

It ranks third because the cutting size is smaller than the ANTTCTIG's yet the price is several times higher. What you pay for is the professional class: sturdier build, repeat-use durability and the kind of tool that vineyards and nurseries run all day. The listing gives no weight, battery or motor details.

Buy it if you prune for income. Skip it if you prune a few shrubs a year.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Electric Pruner, 2 Ah Battery and Charger Included
products.verdict: A V20 platform pruner with a 2 Ah battery and charger included.
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN V20 pruner uses the V20 battery system and comes with a 2 Ah battery and a charger. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It is the sensible pick if you already own V20 tools, since the battery is shared. The kit includes everything needed to start. It ranks fourth because the listing offers no cutting diameter, weight or run time, and it costs more than the ANTTCTIG.

Buy it if you are in the V20 ecosystem. Skip it if you want a stated cut capacity.

products.name: Kebtek Cordless Pruning Shears 25MM Electric Pruners 880G Lightweight
products.verdict: A 25MM cutter weighing 880 grams, for long sessions without wrist fatigue.
products.description:
This Kebtek cuts up to 25MM, about an inch, and weighs 880 grams, roughly 1.9 lbs. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Weight is the stat that wins long days. A pruner heavier than two pounds tires the grip hand within an hour of overhead work. The cost is capacity: an inch is fine for roses, vines and fruit tree twigs and nothing thicker.

Buy it if you prune lots of small stems and want a light tool. Skip it if you tackle branches over an inch.
products.idealFor: Roses, vines and light orchard work.

products.name: Electric Pruning Shears, Upgraded 2.1" Cutting Garden Shears with LCD Display, Brushless Motor Cordless Power Pruner
products.verdict: A 2.1 inch brushless cordless pruner with an LCD display for battery and settings.
products.description:
This pruner cuts up to 2.1 inches, uses a brushless motor and has an LCD display. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Brushless motors run cooler and last longer than brushed ones because there are no carbon brushes to wear. An LCD tells you battery level and mode at a glance. It ranks sixth because the brand is unnamed and the listing offers no battery or warranty detail, making it harder to trust than the ANTTCTIG.

Buy it if you want brushless at a mid price. Skip it if brand support matters.

products.name: Upgraded Electric Pruning Shears, 1.4" Cutting Diameter Cordless Power Pruner with LCD Display, Brushless Motor
products.verdict: A 1.4 inch brushless pruner with an LCD display in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
This pruner cuts up to 1.4 inches, has a brushless motor and an LCD display, and costs the least of the seven.

This is the cheapest way into electric pruning with a brushless motor. The capacity is modest, enough for shrubs, roses and fruit tree twigs. It ranks last because the brand is unnamed and the listing says nothing about battery, blades or warranty.

Buy it if you prune light stems on a tight budget. Skip it if you need thicker cuts.

whatMatters.detail: The rated diameter is for green, live wood. Dry or hard wood cuts thinner. Buy a rating about 25 percent above your thickest regular cut.
Two batteries double your working time, which is why the ANTTCTIG's kit stands out. A 2 Ah pack suits light pruning. Check whether batteries are included or sold separately.
Overhead pruning magnifies every ounce. A tool of 880 grams is comfortable for hours, while a heavy professional unit tires you faster. Listings without weight figures deserve caution.
Brushless motors last longer and run cooler than brushed ones. They cost a little more to make. Both unnamed budget models here list brushless.
Sap and dirt dull blades quickly. Tool-free changes and spare blades keep the tool cutting cleanly. A crushed cut damages the plant.

faq.q: Are electric pruners better than manual ones?
faq.a: For repeated cuts and thick stems, yes. They save your hands and speed up work. For one or two cuts, manual secateurs are quicker.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Trusting the maximum diameter. Dense, dry wood cuts thinner. Choose a rating larger than your usual cut.

faq.q: Is the ANTTCTIG worth it over the BLACK+DECKER?
faq.a: For thick branches and long sessions, yes, thanks to the 2.75 inch cut and second battery. The BLACK+DECKER is easier to maintain and fits an existing platform.
Keep fingers clear of the blade, wear gloves and remove the battery for blade changes. Never cut with the hand holding the branch near the jaws.

faq.q: How often should blades be sharpened?
faq.a: When cuts start crushing instead of slicing. Clean sap off after each session to slow dulling.

faq.q: Can I cut wire or metal?
faq.a: No. The blades are for wood. Cutting wire dulls or chips them.

finalTake: The ANTTCTIG 2.75 inch electric pruner is the best choice for most gardeners, with the largest cut for the money, two batteries and spare blades. The BLACK+DECKER 20V MAX suits owners of other 20V tools, the Kebtek 40MM is for professionals and the 880g Kebtek is for light, long sessions. Choose a cutting size above your thickest branch.
